summary: A 3-page workflow PDF with no narration, so there is no transcript and nothing to correct for Pierre's accent. Page 1 (Overview) covers who repairs. Within 1 year with no misuse, the original seller repairs. After 1 year, or if the customer declares misuse, the Revibe Repair Partner (Revibe Care+) repairs and the original seller doesn't see the claim. It then shows the 4-step flow (customer raises claim in My Account → Revibe agent check → pickup → seller action at Under QC), with pickup AWBs auto-created in AE & ZA and created manually by the seller in SA. It also covers what happens when a pickup fails, what the portal displays (Tracking, Pickup Tracking, Ship-Back, Lab) and that all refunds, credits and charges appear in the payment tool. Page 2 (Seller Decision · Under QC) covers two paths. Valid: the seller repairs, clicks "Repair finished" and the device is shipped back. In SA the seller creates and pays the ship-back AWB; in AE & ZA Revibe creates the AWB and 30 AED is deducted from the seller. It also covers failed deliveries. Invalid: the seller gives a reason + proof and Revibe reviews every Invalid claim. The agent either agrees (device sent to the Lab, AE only, collected by Quiqup) or challenges ("Seller must cover" → Under revision, or "Misuse but customer has RC+" → seller quotation). Lab Valid means the customer is refunded and the device goes back to the seller. Lab Invalid confirms the invalid claim and closes it; in AE Revibe ships the device back, in ZA & SA the customer pays the shipping fees and has 90 days to pay. Outside AE there is no Lab yet and the agent's confirmation of the seller's Invalid is final. Page 3 (Revibe Care+ · Paid Repairs): RC+ covers repairs up to 1,500 AED (Revibe pays the repair); above 1,500 AED the customer pays the difference. Route A: within 1 year, the original seller finds misuse on an RC+ customer. Route B: after 1 year or misuse declared, the device is sent straight to the Revibe Repair Partner. Then come the quotation, agent approval and cost check. At ≤ 1,500 AED Revibe covers the repair and the extended warranty is consumed. Above 1,500 AED the claim waits on customer payment; if not paid, there is no repair, the device is shipped back to the customer and RC+ is cancelled.

unclear.issue: 'Within 1 year' / 'After 1 year' — the document does not say what date the year is counted from.

Step 4 says the seller can see the claim only once the courier delivers it (Under QC). But in SA the seller must create the pickup AWB manually at the Pickup step, before delivery. The document doesn't explain how an SA seller sees or acts on the claim at that stage.
Pickup in SA: the seller creates the pickup AWB manually, but the document does not say who pays for it. It only says the SA seller creates and pays for the ship-back AWB.
Ship-back cost says 'AE & ZA: AWB by Revibe · 30 AED deducted from the seller'. No local-currency amount is given for ZA, so it's unclear whether ZA sellers are charged 30 AED or an equivalent.

Valid claim with failed delivery: 'Yes → seller pays a new AWB' is stated for all markets. In AE & ZA the normal ship-back AWB is made by Revibe with a 30 AED deduction, so it's unclear how the seller pays the new AWB there.

The Lab Invalid box says 'ZA & SA: the customer pays the shipping fees'. But Lab collection is '(AE only)' and outside AE there is 'No Lab yet'. It's unclear whether this rule applies after the agent's final Invalid confirmation in ZA & SA.
'Stripe code entered once paid' — the document does not say who enters the Stripe code or where.
'90 days to pay' — the document does not say what happens if the customer doesn't pay the shipping fees within 90 days.

Lab Valid → 'customer refunded' and the device goes back to the seller. The document does not say whether the refund is charged to the seller; it only says all refunds, credits and charges appear in the payment tool.

Route A says 'Revibe covers the cost' of the original seller's repair. It doesn't say whether the 1,500 AED cap and the customer-pays-the-difference step also apply to Route A, although the Quotation section appears under both routes.
The ship-back cost for RC+ repairs (who creates and pays the ship-back AWB, including a new attempt after a failed delivery) is not stated.
